verdict.rationale: Morph documents high-throughput generation for its specialized models: Fast Apply at 10,500+ tok/s, Compact at 33,000 tok/s, and Reflex classifiers labeling a turn in ~90ms. Prefix caching is on for every open source model, and dedicated endpoints let you reserve capacity. The throughput numbers cover the specialized tools rather than general chat generation, and nothing quantifies time-to-first-token. Missing for 10: documented TTFT or latency figures for the general chat models (e.g. Kimi K3), throughput figures for general chat generation, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the speed claims.

support.subject: As a developer, I can serve latency-sensitive workloads with fast time-to-first-token and high-throughput generation

citations.quote: Fast Apply merges just the changed lines at 10,500 tok/s, 98% accuracy.
Drop filler from chat history and code context at 33,000 tok/s.
Small text classifiers that label a turn in ~90ms
Prefix caching is on for every open source model. No configuration, no cache-write surcharge.
Reserve model capacity by choosing a model and plan. Morph provisions and operates it
